full_scan.scope: every output of the 4 OCR models for each of the 767 crops: 3068 outputs
full_scan.method: searched for answer-key text: number-letter pairs as a key prints them ('1-C 2-C'; a number, then on the same line a dash, dot, colon, bracket or slash, then a lone letter A to E), space-separated pairs in runs of three or more consecutive numbers, and key wording ('cevap anahtarı', 'doğru cevap', 'Cevap: C'); each pair also checked against the answer key printed on the crop's page (answer_observations) and against the crop's own question's number and answer

conditions.A: clean text: the published text-track run (the same questions, prompts and options), graded against the bank as it stands now
conditions.B: the crop(s), passage first, as the whole state; instructions 'Which option is correct?'; the question's own option letters as the choices, each described by its letter only
conditions.C: condition A's text and options, with the crop(s) after the text; A's instructions ('Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question?')
conditions.D: one OCR model's output for the crop(s) (passage first, joined by a blank line) as the state, as its official export gives it, with layout tags removed (Unlimited-OCR-2's block boxes and page marks) and markup kept; instructions 'Which option is correct?'; option letters only, as B

measures_method.accuracy: right answers over the 763 questions; a refusal or an answer outside the options counts as wrong
measures_method.ece_brier_auroc: benchmark_metrics: ECE over 10 equal bins of the chosen option's probability, Brier score of that probability, AUROC of right against wrong answers; answers without a probability are left out of these three
measures_method.ece_interval: 95% percentile interval over 4000 cluster bootstrap resamples (questions sharing a passage form one cluster), numpy default_rng(0); the same draws for every condition
measures_method.at_0_99: answers whose chosen option has probability at least 0.99, right and wrong
measures_method.paired: exact McNemar test on accuracy (benchmark_metrics.paired_comparison, with its 95% interval of the difference) and a paired bootstrap on ECE (4000 resamples, the same draws for both sides)

ocr.reference: the bank's clean text (condition A's text): the passage for a passage crop; the stem and the options written as printed ('A) ...') for a question crop
ocr.cer_method: Levenshtein distance between the normalised OCR text and the normalised reference, over the reference's length, summed over all 767 crops (micro average); the median per-crop CER is also given. Normalisation, both texts: NFC, HTML entities decoded, HTML tags, LaTeX wrappers (argument kept), Markdown emphasis, heading marks and math delimiters removed, typographic quotes, dashes and the ellipsis unified, whitespace collapsed; OCR text only: layout tags (Unlimited-OCR-2's block boxes and page marks; see ocr_text), a leading printed question number and line-end hyphens inside words removed. Case and Turkish letters are kept as they are. Headers the crop shows but the bank does not hold (a passage's 'questions 4-5' line, the publisher's margin text) count as insertions, and so does a different placement of the numerals printed under underlined words, which the bank writes inline as '(I)' after the words
ocr.turkish_method: from the character alignment behind the CER (rapidfuzz Levenshtein.editops): an edit counts for a letter group when the reference character or the OCR character is in it (ı/i/İ/I share one group; ş, ğ, ç, ö, ü each with its capital); substitutions, deletions and insertions all count. 'dotless_dotted' counts ı<->i and İ<->I swaps; 'diacritic_dropped' counts ş->s, ğ->g, ç->c, ö->o, ü->u (either case)
ocr.marked_method: underlined words: each <u>...</u> span of the reference (stem, options and passage) counts once; it is marked when the OCR text wraps the same words in any markup (HTML u, ins, b, strong, em, i, mark, s or span; Markdown **, __, *, _, ++ or ==; LaTeX underline, uline, uwave, dotuline, underbrace, textbf, textit or emph; or a combining low line under the letters), the wrapped text containing the span within twice its length plus 10 characters, or lying inside the span and covering at least half of it. Numbered words: each numeral marker of the reference stem or passage ('(I)' inline or 'I.' at a line start) counts once; per numeral, the OCR text marks as many as the standalone tokens of that numeral it holds (any brackets or none; Unicode Roman numerals read as letters) beyond the ones the options hold, up to the reference's count

chandra-ocr-2.method: chandra-ocr 0.2.0 official vLLM path (chandra.model.InferenceManager(method='vllm'), the code behind the `chandra <input> <out> --method vllm` CLI) against a vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev613+g8977b13a1 OpenAI-compatible server (local nightly venv on 1 GPU, started with the same arguments as chandra's `chandra_vllm` launcher: --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 18000 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-kwargs {min_pixels: 3136, max_pixels: 6291456}; the launcher itself would run the vllm/vllm-openai:v0.17.0 docker image, which was not used). Each crop was loaded with chandra.input.load_image (upscaled so the shorter side is >= 1536 px), resized by chandra's scale_to_fit, sent as PNG with the default 'ocr_layout' prompt (PROMPT_MAPPING['ocr_layout']); all 767 requests in one generate() call with 64 client threads. Decoding: temperature 0, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 12384 (chandra defaults); chandra's built-in retry re-generates an output with a detected repeat-token loop at temperature min(0.2*(n+1), 0.8), top_p 0.95 (up to 6 retries). The model emits layout HTML (<div data-bbox data-label> blocks); the stored text is chandra's official markdown export (BatchOutputItem.markdown = chandra.output.parse_markdown with the CLI defaults include_images=True, include_headers_footers=False, i.e. Page-Header/Page-Footer blocks dropped). dtype bfloat16. In this run chandra's client logged 39 repeat-token retry events (the retried pages' final text therefore comes from a sampled, non-greedy re-generation; chandra does not report which pages).
chandra-ocr-2.prompt:
OCR this image to HTML, arranged as layout blocks. Each layout block should be a div with the data-bbox attribute representing the bounding box of the block in x0 y0 x1 y1 format. Bboxes are normalized 0-1000. The data-label attribute is the label for the block. Use the following labels: - Caption - Footnote - Equation-Block - List-Group - Page-Header - Page-Footer - Image - Section-Header - Table - Text - Complex-Block - Code-Block - Form - Table-Of-Contents - Figure - Chemical-Block - Diagram - Bibliography - Blank-Page Only use these tags ['math', 'br', 'i', 'b', 'u', 'del', 'sup', 'sub', 'table', 'tr', 'td', 'p', 'th', 'div', 'pre', 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'ul', 'ol', 'li', 'input', 'a', 'span', 'img', 'hr', 'tbody', 'small', 'caption', 'strong', 'thead', 'big', 'code', 'chem'], and these attributes ['class', 'colspan', 'rowspan', 'display', 'checked', 'type', 'border', 'value', 'style', 'href', 'alt', 'align', 'data-bbox', 'data-label']. Guidelines: * Inline math: Surround math with ... tags. Math expressions should be rendered in KaTeX-compatible LaTeX. Use display for block math. * Tables: Use colspan and rowspan attributes to match table structure. * Formatting: Maintain consistent formatting with the image, including spacing, indentation, subscripts/superscripts, and special characters. * Images: Include a description of any images in the alt attribute of an tag. Do not fill out the src property. Describe in detail inside the div tag. Also convert charts to high fidelity data, and convert diagrams to mermaid. * Forms: Mark checkboxes and radio buttons properly. * Text: join lines together properly into paragraphs using

...

tags. Use
tags for line breaks within paragraphs, but only when absolutely necessary to maintain meaning. * Chemistry: Use ... tags for chemical formulas with reactive SMILES. * Lists: Preserve indents and proper list markers. * Use the simplest possible HTML structure that accurately represents the content of the block. * Make sure the text is accurate and easy for a human to read and interpret. Reading order should be correct and natural.

dots-mocr.method: dots_mocr parser (github.com/rednote-hilab/dots.mocr @ 23f3e5612fb8, installed editable) official vLLM path: DotsMOCRParser.parse_file(<png>, prompt_mode='prompt_layout_all_en', fitz_preprocess=True), i.e. `python3 dots_mocr/parser.py <png>` with the CLI defaults (prompt_layout_all_en, top_p 1.0, max_completion_tokens 16384, dpi 200 fitz re-render of the image, no min/max_pixels override) except temperature 0.0 instead of the CLI's 0.1 for greedy decoding; requests go to a vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev613+g8977b13a1 OpenAI-compatible server (local nightly venv, native DotsOCRForCausalLM implementation, launched as in the model card: --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --chat-template-content-format string --served-model-name model --trust-remote-code; model dtype bfloat16 from config). 64 images in flight. The parser's request function was replaced by an identical copy that also records finish_reason (to detect token-limit hits). The model returns layout JSON (bbox, category, text); the stored text is the parser's own markdown export (<name>.md = format_transformer.layoutjson2md(..., no_page_hf=False): cells in reading order joined by blank lines, Formula as LaTeX, Table as HTML, Picture cells as an inline base64 PNG image link); when the JSON fails to parse, the parser's OutputCleaner fallback text is stored (noted in failures).
dots-mocr.prompt:
Please output the layout information from the PDF image, including each layout element's bbox, its category, and the corresponding text content within the bbox.

1. Bbox format: [x1, y1, x2, y2]

2. Layout Categories: The possible categories are ['Caption', 'Footnote', 'Formula', 'List-item', 'Page-footer', 'Page-header', 'Picture', 'Section-header', 'Table', 'Text', 'Title'].

3. Text Extraction & Formatting Rules:
    - Picture: For the 'Picture' category, the text field should be omitted.
    - Formula: Format its text as LaTeX.
    - Table: Format its text as HTML.
    - All Others (Text, Title, etc.): Format their text as Markdown.

4. Constraints:
    - The output text must be the original text from the image, with no translation.
    - All layout elements must be sorted according to human reading order.

5. Final Output: The entire output must be a single JSON object.

surya-ocr-2.method: surya-ocr 0.22.1 official full-page OCR path (the code behind `surya_ocr <folder>`: surya.input.load.load_from_folder, then RecognitionPredictor(SuryaInferenceManager())(images, full_page=True)) against a vLLM 0.20.1 OpenAI-compatible server (vllm==0.20.1 from PyPI in an isolated venv on 1 GPU, the version of surya's vllm/vllm-openai:v0.20.1 docker image, started with the same arguments surya's VllmBackend gives that image for VLLM_GPU_TYPE=h100: --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 18000 --max-num-seqs 104 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-kwargs {min_pixels: 3136, max_pixels: 6291456} --speculative-config {method: mtp, num_speculative_tokens: 2}; docker itself was not used). The server venv pins transformers 5.17.0 (surya requires >=5.12.1): transformers >=5.18 loads this checkpoint's char-level tokenizer as the byte-level Qwen3_5Tokenizer, which corrupted every prompt and turned non-ASCII output letters (ı ğ ç ö ü ...) into U+FFFD/control bytes in a first run with vLLM nightly + transformers 5.20 (discarded). Attached via SURYA_INFERENCE_BACKEND=vllm, SURYA_INFERENCE_URL; client concurrency 96 (surya default for that sizing). Each crop is sent once as PNG (after surya's scale_to_fit) with the default full-page prompt HIGH_ACCURACY_BBOX_PROMPT; decoding: temperature 0, top_p 0.1, max_tokens 12288 (surya defaults; SURYA_FULLPAGE_REGEN off), surya's client retries a request that ends in a repeat-token loop at temperature min(0.2*(n+1), 0.8), top_p 0.95 (max 3 retries), and a page whose full-page HTML fails to parse or loops falls back to surya's layout + per-block OCR. The model emits HTML layout blocks (<div data-bbox data-label>); surya parses them into PageOCRResult.blocks in reading order with per-block inner HTML. Surya has no markdown/text export of its own (that lives in marker), so the stored text is the non-skipped blocks' `html` (surya's official per-block output, math in <math>, tables as <table>) joined in reading order with blank lines; bounding boxes and labels are dropped. dtype bfloat16. In this run: 101 client-side retry requests (non-greedy), 101 of them full-page; 2 pages used the layout + per-block fallback (12 layout/block requests).
surya-ocr-2.prompt: OCR this image to HTML. Each block is a div with data-label and data-bbox (x0 y0 x1 y1, normalized 0-1000).

unlimited-ocr-2.method: Model card's Transformers path (trust_remote_code; the snapshot's modeling_unlimitedocr.py), README 'Single-page inference': AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True, use_safetensors=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval().cuda(), then model.infer(tokenizer, image_file=<png>, output_path=<dir>, save_results=True) per crop with all decoding defaults: prompt built automatically as '<PAGE><image>Multi page parsing.' for one page, crop_mode=None -> gundam dynamic tiling for a single page (base_size 1024, image_size 640, max_crops 16), greedy argmax (temperature 0), PageCountGuard on with max_page_tokens=20000, max_length 131072, no n-gram blocking, DASH sparse attention (dash_topm 16). eval_mode=True only disables the console token streamer; return_dict=True only returns token ids/finish reason. Batch size 1 per model copy (the path has no batching); 8 worker processes, each with its own model copy, shared GPU 2 and took the crops round-robin; seconds = first worker start (after all models loaded) to last worker end. The model emits markdown with grounding refs (<|ref|>..<|/ref|><|det|>[[boxes]]<|/det|>) and a <PAGE> marker; the stored text is the model's own save_results output result.md (its _uocr_save_results: non-image refs/boxes removed, image refs replaced by ![](images/page_0_<i>.jpg) links, '<PAGE>' line kept). torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 4.52.1, dtype bfloat16.

ocr.verified: the human-verified subset: the crops of the questions whose text was checked by hand (status 'verified' in the bank), 375 of 763 questions, 378 crops with their passages

cost.basis: the retained responses only: one per question and cell ('requests' counts them); not every attempt and not an invoice; see requests

recorded_client_retries.source: the runs' console logs: HTTP 503 from OpenAI's Decisions API in runs 4 and 9 (GPT-6 Luna, B and C) and HTTP 500 from the d3 server in run 34 (vLLM-SR d3-ultra, D with Unlimited-OCR-2), each retried by the runner

notes: A cell with two run records was resumed after an interruption: the second run asked only the questions the first had left unanswered. These are continuations, not repeats.

The answer table keeps one row per question and cell, so an attempt that failed and was asked again is not stored. Client retries are known only from the runs' console logs, which do not cover every run. Retained answers plus recorded retries is a lower bound on the requests sent, not a complete count.
Tokens and costs come from the retained responses only. They are not every attempt and not an invoice; the usage and cost of attempts that were not retained are unknown, not zero.
'failures' lists requests still without a stored answer when these measures ran. An empty list does not mean that no request ever failed.
